prediction_ref.short_label: Agent-builder frameworks ship sandboxed MCP tool execution by default by Q1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Today's news is a direct forcing signal: Obsidian Security's working proof-of-concept for the Flowise Custom-MCP RCE (CVE-2026-40933) lands in the stdio transport, which launches a user-supplied command as an unsandboxed child process, so a poisoned exported workflow executes on import with no approval prompt. The sharper beat is that researchers showed the official patch can be bypassed and self-hosted installs stay vulnerable by default, so the recommended fix moves from patch-and-wait to disabling stdio in favor of Server-Sent Events and treating imported MCP configs as untrusted code. A coordinated MCP supply-chain advisory ties the same unsandboxed-subprocess root cause across LiteLLM, Agent Zero, LangBot, and Windsurf, which is exactly the structural pressure toward sandboxed-by-default MCP tool execution this prediction names.
